stem.en: Which process normally helps stop tumours from forming in animal tissues, and do plant cells show it?

text.en: Osmosis; plant cells do not show it at all.

feedback.en: Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane. It does not stop division, and plant cells do show it.

text.en: Contact inhibition; plant cells do not show it.

feedback.en: Yes. Cells stop dividing when they touch, and rigid plant walls change this.

text.en: Meiosis; plant cells show it only in their roots.

feedback.en: Meiosis makes gametes. It does not stop tumours.

text.en: Contact inhibition; plant cells show it even more strongly.

feedback.en: Rigid cell walls mean plant cells do not show contact inhibition.

explanation.en: Contact inhibition stops division when cells touch their neighbours, and cancer cells lose it. Plant cells do not show it, because their rigid walls give them a different pattern of growth. Plants can still form abnormal growths called galls, often started by insects, mites or bacteria.
